clue.text: Recruit acted badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of acted are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A new recruit turned in a poor performance on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a trainee officer, a new entrant to a service.

clue.text: Double over and collapse

explanation.surface: Someone doubles up and falls in a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: To fold up is to bend in half like a sheet folded, and also to fail or give way, as a business folds.

clue.text: Interview everybody in the theatre

explanation.surface: An interview given to the whole house at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal meeting with a monarch or pope is granted as an audience, and the spectators at a show are collectively its audience.

clue.text: No quick-growing plant?

parts.note: a climbing plant that trails along walls, whose name also suggests something that moves slowly rather than fast

explanation.surface: A gardener asks about a slow-growing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy and similar climbers are known by a name that also means one who goes slowly.

clue.text: West Indian preserve has first-class container

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
A1 means first-class, with the figure 1 read as the letter I
a can is a tin container

explanation.surface: Caribbean jam sold in a top-quality jar.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the Caribbean island whose capital is Kingston is a West Indian.

clue.text: Drive off on vehicle, we hear? This helps to stop it

indicators.note: on places one piece next to the other in the down entry

parts.note: a brake is an old horse-drawn carriage, as in shooting brake

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for drive off is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: to shoo is to drive away an animal

explanation.surface: A driver speeds off in a car that seems to need a way to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns SHOO into its sound-alike SHOE.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved block pressed against a wheel is a stopping device on a vehicle.

clue.text: Work on island plot

indicators.note: on puts the work after the island in the across entry

parts.note: the Isle of Man, often just Man in crosswords
an oeuvre is a body of work by an artist

explanation.surface: Labour on an island allotment.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme or crafty move is a plot.

clue.text: Gormless mountain dog

indicators.note: read as gorm-less: the letters gorm are removed from the mountain

parts.note: Cairn Gorm is a peak in the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: A stupid dog from the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gormless' (British for dim-witted) is read as 'without GORM', so CAIRNGORM loses GORM.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn terrier is a small Scottish breed of dog.

clue.text: This man gets a seat

parts.note: a man's name which, with man added, makes a cushioned seat or footstool

explanation.surface: A man finds himself a place to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name that, followed by the word man, gives a padded couch.

clue.text: Closing date for journalist's dull column

parts.note: dead can mean dull or lifeless
a line is a row or column, as of soldiers

explanation.surface: A reporter's boring column has to be filed by the cut-off date.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-off time for copy is what reporters work to.

clue.text: One is going to make them

definitions.text: One is going to make them

parts.words: One is going to make them
parts.note: anyone walking or travelling leaves footprints or marks behind

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to create something.
explanation.definitionFit: Footprints and trails are left by a person moving along.

clue.text: Worked at the wheel for a stretch?

explanation.surface: Did someone drive for a long while?
explanation.definitionFit: Span is the past tense of spin, as at a spinning wheel, and also a length or extent.

clue.text: Put ban on spirits and remove without alternative

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cut-out word goes round the other

parts.note: to excise is to cut out
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Prohibit alcohol and drop the alternatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: EXCISE goes round OR. The surface plays on excise duty on alcoholic spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving out ghosts or demons forbids their presence.

clue.text: Risk coming over river

indicators.note: over places the first piece above the second in the down entry

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A gamble crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazardous undertaking is a venture or risk.

clue.text: Made work play, perhaps

explanation.surface: A drama has been changed so that it functions.
explanation.definitionFit: Altered to suit means made to function, and a stage version of a novel is an example of something reworked.

clue.text: A girl not without heart, but peevishly impatient

parts.note: Petula is a girl's name, as in the singer Petula Clark

indicators.note: without heart means the middle letter of not is dropped, keeping its outside pair

explanation.surface: A girl who is not heartless, yet is cross and irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: A sulky, irritable person behaves in a peevish, impatient way.

clue.text: Ghost seen in Hampton maze

indicators.note: maze suggests the letters of Hampton are twisted about into a new path

explanation.surface: A spectre spotted in the famous hedge maze at Hampton Court.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampton Court is a royal palace near London with a famous hedge maze.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre or apparition is a ghost.

clue.text: Fair and square, initially, in accommodation

indicators.note: in puts the conjunction and the square's first letter inside the lodging

parts.note: home is where one is accommodated
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of square

explanation.surface: Being fair and square in housing matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the sense of good-looking is a synonym.

clue.text: Train wedging an old coin between the points

indicators.note: between puts the coin in the middle, with one compass point either side

parts.note: two E for East, compass points
a ducat is an old gold coin used in Europe

explanation.surface: A railway coach with a coin jammed between the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wedging' supports 'between': the coin is jammed between two E's.
explanation.definitionFit: To teach or instruct someone is to train them.

clue.text: Stockman here and there, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters of and there might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A cattle farmer moving about the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' points at the fodder that follows: 'and there', perhaps, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A herdsman who tends cattle is an archaic term for a stockman.

clue.text: Raise the stake for mount hotly tipped when it runs

definitions.text: mount hotly tipped when it runs

indicators.note: raise in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an ante is the stake put in before a poker hand

explanation.surface: A gambler ups the bet on a racehorse that is the hot favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a volcano in Sicily: its lava runs hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano is a mountain that is literally hot at its tip when its lava flows.

clue.text: Architect helped make Brighton a showpiece

indicators.note: helped make indicates the letters form part of the run Brighton a showpiece

explanation.surface: An architect helped turn Brighton into a showplace.
explanation.walkthrough: John Nash designed the Royal Pavilion in Brighton, an English seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash was a Regency architect.

clue.text: Reorganised Delhi's defence

indicators.note: reorganised signals the letters of Delhi's, including the s, are rearranged

explanation.surface: India's capital has restructured its military.
explanation.definitionFit: A shield is a piece of armour used for protection.

clue.text: It's loud for a musical note

parts.note: taken as written
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Playing loudly for one particular note.
explanation.definitionFit: In music forte is the instruction to play loudly.

clue.text: Somehow lost on points wrongly taken away

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: E and N, East and North, compass points

explanation.surface: A boxer somehow lost a decision on points and feels robbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken unlawfully is the meaning of stolen.

clue.text: Very strong players at club

parts.note: the cast are the players in a show
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: Actors at a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbreakable or rigid, like an iron alibi, is very strong.

clue.text: Doctor may take one for an idler

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor might take on a lazy patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A male bee does no work, so a lazy person is called one.

clue.text: Fan fire?

explanation.surface: Is a fan a type of fire?
explanation.definitionFit: To fan flames or to fire up someone both mean to rouse or arouse.
